page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 AMD processor, the instance provisions 24 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The architecture does not include dedicated graphics processing units, centering compute and memory resources strictly on core system throughput.

A defining component of this instance configuration is its massive bundled local storage, featuring 17,280 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity. This direct-attached NVMe array provides high-density, low-latency disk access for data-heavy workloads without relying entirely on remote network storage volumes. In addition, the instance supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk configurations, although complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

From a cost-efficiency and architecture standpoint, bundling over 17 TB of local NVMe storage alongside a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio offers high resource density on a single node. The trade-off is the ephemeral nature typical of direct-attached instance storage, which demands application-level replication or persistent backup architectures to protect against node termination.

The hardware profile makes the L24aos_v5 well configured for large transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores like Apache Cassandra or MongoDB, big data processing engines, real-time analytics, and data warehousing setups that require vast local caching and high IOPS density.
description: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for high-density transactional and analytical workloads. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the instance features an x86_64 AMD processor supplying 24 dedicated vCPUs, 192.0 GB of system RAM, and zero hardware GPUs. With an 8.0 GB memory-per-core ratio, it pairs robust memory capacity with 17,280 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The massive local solid-state footprint enables high input/output processing for I/O-intensive database engines and large data processing pipelines without incurring remote storage overhead. While the local NVMe storage provides superior throughput and latency, its ephemeral characteristics require fault-tolerant data clustering or external Premium Storage volumes for persistent states. Consequently, the L24aos_v5 functions as a dense, cost-effective computational node for relational databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, Elasticsearch clusters, and high-capacity data warehousing applications.
